title: Orchestration playbook: milestone safeguards and release exit criteria for API/Console/Runtime
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Objective: Create a single, pragmatic playbook that defines milestone safeguards, scope-lock invariants, and explicit release-exit criteria for the coordinated API / Console / Runtime release train. This ticket captures the cross-team choreography, required artifacts, and gating signals so engineering, design, SRE and GTM have a single source of truth for go/no-go decisions.

Principles: Keep scope lock minimal and testable; prefer signal-driven gating (telemetry + smoke tests) over subjective signoff; make rollback and fallback plans explicit; align release notes and customer comms with feature-level risk categories.

Scope:
- Define milestone checkpoints (Feature Complete, QA Freeze, Canary Ramp, Wide Rollout) with concrete deliverables and owners.
- Formalize 'scope-lock invariants' — what cannot change after a checkpoint without re-approval (API contract changes, model-variant swaps, CLI flags, billing/quotas).
- Establish exit/gate criteria for each milestone: tests, telemetry thresholds, dependency readiness, docs, and release notes.
- Create a compact release-notes coordination template and schedule tied to milestones.
- Draft runbook for canary ramp and automated rollback conditions.
- Document cross-team responsibilities, notification flows, and artifacts (PRs, design mocks, eval dashboards, telemetry links).

Milestone definitions and deliverables:
1) Feature Complete (T-21 days): code merged to release branch; API schema diffs documented; design mocks finalized; PRs linked to ticket; release-notes draft created. Owner: Eng PM.
2) QA Freeze (T-10 days): all blocking tests passing; automated e2e smoke suite green; performance baseline (p50/p95 token latency) captured; security checklist completed. No nontrivial API surface changes after this point without repo-level approval. Owner: QA Lead.
3) Canary Ramp (T-5 to T+3 days): staged traffic to Canary pool (hosted/dedicated/private variants); key telemetry (errors, latencies, cost per token, model accuracy regression) monitored; automated alerts and rollback hooks enabled. Owner: SRE/Runtime.
4) Wide Rollout (T+4 days): gradual ramp to full cohort based on canary health. Communications: release notes published, customer comms segmented by risk. Owner: GTM Lead.

Scope-lock invariants (examples):
- Breaking API changes (schema removals, renamed fields) prohibited post-Feature Complete without cross-team emergency approval.
- Model architecture swaps (e.g., quantization mode change that affects outputs) require explicit QA signoff and regression tests.
- Billing, quota, or pricing parameter changes require Finance + Legal review.

Exit (gate) criteria checklist (each gate requires green or documented exception):
- All mandatory CI jobs passed for 48 hours on release branch.
- Critical e2e smoke tests (auth, generation, embeddings, streaming) pass at least twice in the last 24 hours.
- Performance regressions: p95 tail latency within 15% of baseline AND unit cost < 1.2x baseline for typical token profiles; otherwise must attach mitigation plan.
- Error budget: service error rate below 0.1% or justified mitigation in place.
- Release notes draft completed with feature-level risk tags and owner for each entry.
- Security checklist: SSO/KMS changes approved if applicable.
- Observability: dashboards and log retention configured for 14+ days for initial rollout.

Release notes coordination:
- Owners produce feature-level bullets by Feature Complete. Each bullet must include: product area, short description, risk tag (low/medium/high), migration notes, and contact.
- One consolidated release notes doc generated and reviewed in a cross-functional sync at QA Freeze.
- GTM email/social templates prepared during Canary Ramp; legal/compliance signoff required for customer-impacting changes.

Telemetry and SLO gating:
- Define key metrics: token throughput, p50/p95 latency, error rate (per endpoint), cost/unit, eval-quality delta for model changes.
- Attach dashboards links and alert thresholds to the milestone artifact.
- Canary must sustain SLOs for 72 hours with automated rollbacks configured for priority alerts.

Rollback and fallback strategy:
- Automatic rollback triggers: sustained p95 > 2x baseline for 10 minutes, sustained error rate > 1% for 5 minutes, or quality regression above defined threshold for model-output monitors.
- Manual rollback path and owner list in runbook; ensure config flag to serve previous model/version is vetted and smoke-tested.

Communications and GTM:
- Weekly triage + milestone sync cadence starting at T-28 days.
- Standups shift to daily during Canary Ramp and Wide Rollout.
- Release notes owner to publish staged drafts to internal Slack channel and Confluence page.
- Customer comms playbook prepared for high-risk items with targeted outreach lists.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Last-minute API contract change. Mitigation: enforce PR gating and require PM-level exception log plus owner pairing to QA.
- Risk: Model quality regression after quantization update. Mitigation: preflight eval harness and hold-out prompt sets tied to regression alerts.
- Risk: Observability gaps. Mitigation: pre-rollout checklist must include dashboard and alert verification by SRE.

Deliverables:
- One-page playbook summarizing milestones and gates (to be embedded in the release Confluence page).
- Release-notes template and populated draft.
- Canary runbook with automated rollback rules and escalation matrix.
- Cross-team owner roster and notification runbook.

Acceptance criteria:
- Playbook doc created and approved by Eng, SRE, Design, Legal, and GTM.
- Release-notes template used to produce first draft by Feature Complete.
- Canary runbook validated in a dry-run (staging canary) and rollback path executed once.
- At least one cross-functional milestone sync recorded with issues and owners assigned.

Success metrics (post-release):
- Time to detect critical regressions during canary < 10 minutes.
- Percent of releases that require emergency rollback < 5% in first quarter after adoption.
- Reduction in ambiguous go/no-go escalations vs prior release train (target -50%).
